topic: Citation management and source tracking for knowledge bases
query: research citation management source tracking knowledge base
title: Best Reference Managers and Citation Tools for Research (2026)
snippet: Citation managers such as EndNote, Mendeley, or Zotero are software tools for keeping track of your sources that allow you to collect and store information about sources, organize and keep track of your references, create a shared library for group projects, and automatically generate citations and reference lists in the style of your choice.
claim: Citation management tools track source information, organize references, and generate formatted citations to prevent scholarly attribution errors.

topic: Evidence-based documentation and source attribution best practices
query: evidence-based documentation best practices source attribution
title: Source Documentation Best Practices: The Foundation of Research Data
snippet: Ethical research and writing means giving proper attribution and credit to the work of others, as the ideas, words, and publications of others are considered intellectual property in the academic community. Citing sources without reading them is considered fraudulent because you are lying about the work you have done.
claim: Source documentation requires verifying sources were actually read and properly crediting intellectual property to avoid fraudulent citation.

query: knowledge base fact verification methodology fact checking
title: Automated Fact-Checking: A Survey
snippet: A fact is defined as a triple that has the form of ("subject" s, "predicate" p, "object" o), and natural language processing techniques are used to convert a textual claim into a structured format. The pipelines usually consist of evidence retrieval and verification.
claim: Fact verification uses structured knowledge base queries to retrieve supporting evidence and validate claims through NLP-based evidence retrieval.

topic: Research record schema structure and design
title: A General Pipeline for Digesting Scientific Literature into a Shared Scientific Knowledge Base
snippet: The database schema is the intellectual heart of systems that digest research information, encoding domain knowledge such that captured information becomes useful and determines which comparisons across publications are enabled.
claim: Schema design determines what research comparisons are possible by encoding domain knowledge about how information relates across sources.

topic: Source attribution and quote verification in generated content
query: source attribution quote verification fact verification systems
title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents
snippet: Citation hallucination rates range from 11% to 57% across commercially deployed models. Sentence-level attribution systems can attribute each sentence in generated text to quotes from source documents, allowing for quick fact-checking.
claim: Sentence-level attribution systems can map generated content back to source quotes to verify citations and prevent hallucination.

topic: Fact-checking and source provenance verification methods
query: fact-checking and source provenance verification methods
title: Fact-Checking & Verification – Global Investigative Journalism Network
snippet: A widely-used framework involves 'five pillars of verification:' provenance, source, date, location, and motivation. To verify a source, you can check the author by researching their credentials to ensure they are qualified to discuss the topic. Additionally, you should identify if the platform publishing the information is known for accuracy and reliability.
claim: Systematic verification uses five pillars (provenance, source, date, location, motivation) with cross-checking against multiple reliable sources.

topic: Semantic search and snippet extraction from knowledge graphs
query: semantic search snippet extraction knowledge graphs
title: The future of knowledge graph: Will structured and semantic search become one?
snippet: Knowledge graphs are the ideal format to map and store the relationships and meaning to enable semantic search. Semantic search gives engines the information needed to understand the meaning and intent behind user queries, rather than relying solely on keyword matching.
claim: Knowledge graphs enable semantic search by storing entity relationships and attributes, allowing queries based on meaning rather than keywords alone.

topic: Knowledge graph fact recording and schema patterns
query: knowledge graph fact recording schema design
title: Knowledge Graph Schema Design Patterns and Principles
snippet: Knowledge graphs store information as triplets (subject, predicate, object), and the entire 'blueprint' that defines the KG's structure is its schema, which specifies the different node types, edge types, properties, and constraints. It's very common to have a resource that has a source that needs to be recorded to understand how information was obtained.
claim: Knowledge graph schemas define structure through triplets and require recording source provenance for each recorded fact.
